language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
G’day mates, my name is Tess.
We are having a music program featuring my friends and I here in the music center. We need to solve some problems today.
For example, on the stage there are 24 chairs. How many ways can we arrange the chairs
so that there are equal numbers of chairs on each row?
Well, it’s not as hard as it looks. You just have to remember that is factoring problem.
Here are some factors of 24 that my friends came up with.
Lily said: 1 row of 24 chairs = 1 x 24 = 24
Jack said: 2 rows of 12 chairs = 2 x 12 = 24
Cooper said: 3 rows of 8 chairs = 3 x 8 = 24
Ruby said: 4 rows of 6 chairs = 4 x 6 = 24
This means the factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4 , 6, 8, 12, and 24.
When we multiply two factors numbers together we get a number called a multiple.
In this case, our product is 24 chairs.
Remember, factors are numbers and can be divided into a whole number without any remainder.
5 rows of chair wouldn’t work because 5 can’t divide into 24. It would leave a remainder.
